A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same COPE research paper, with 21 readable pages including Appendices A–L. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching scientific content, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on five personalized generation tasks in Table 1, alongside model comparisons, ablations and further empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original experimental results, including the five-task evaluation, component ablations and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same contrastive decoding procedure, implicit reward, PEFT personalization and DPO training with synthetic negatives. Equations 1–6 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate News Headline and Scholarly Title Generation from LaMP, and Abstract Generation, Review Writing and Topic Writing from LongLaMP. No training or evaluation coverage changes.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons in Tables 1, 2 and 5–7 retain Base, RAG, PAG, TAM and OPPU. Comparator membership in the ablation and supplementary analyses also matches.

E3.justification: The selection of 100 users with the longest histories, evaluation metrics, model configurations, training budgets and decoding settings are unchanged, including appendix protocols.

E4.justification: Both retain the CD/DPO ablations, Figure 3 sensitivity analysis, implicit-reward validation, perplexity analysis, user-heterogeneity analysis and qualitative examples. No analysis is added, removed or revised.

E5.justification: Appendix H retains the same standard errors across test samples and confidence-interval discussion. Standard-deviation reporting in Table 10 and sampling information in Appendix D are also unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples match. For example, Table 1 reports COPE Abstract Generation ROUGE-1 of 0.392 and ROUGE-L of 0.239 in both versions; appendix results are likewise identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning in Section 3 and the RLHF/DPO derivations in Appendix I are identical. No assumptions, proofs or formal properties are revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about decoding-time personalization, implicit rewards without external reward models, performance and applicability across LLMs.

C2.justification: Interpretations of personalization gains, component interactions, fluency and robustness are unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning uniform user hyperparameters and evaluation restricted to LoRA.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, retrieval details, prompts, chat templates and code-access information match in Section 4.1 and the appendices. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations and the bibliography are unchanged, including positioning relative to personalization, contrastive decoding, reward-guided decoding and preference learning.

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv v2 dated 26 September 2025 to v3 dated 24 November 2025. The title, authors, prose, terminology and document structure remain identical.

P2.justification: All nine figures and thirteen tables retain their content, captions, formatting and placement. Rendered pages 2–21 are pixel-identical; page 1 differs only in the version/date stamp, without a layout change.

improvement.justification: The only visible revision is the arXiv version/date stamp, with its corresponding hyperlink updated. Scientific content, evidence, explanations and reproducibility information remain identical throughout the main paper and appendices, establishing no meaningful difference in overall quality.
